items.text: Christa Pike likely has ‘brain injury’ after botched execution — here’s what went wrong
items.article: Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike likely suffered a brain injury after surviving two lethal injection doses during a botched execution. See more of our coverage in your search results. Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike will likely have brain damage after her botched execution , during which she chillingly lifted her head and asked if the pain she was feeling was normal. Pike, 50, was rushed to the hospital Wednesday after the Tennessee Department of Corrections administered two doses of the highly potent sedative, Pentobarbital, but it failed to kill her. The murderer, who was sentenced to death for the monstrous 1995 slaying of a classmate, was “being provided life-saving measures” in the hospital, her lawyers said – but she likely has a brain injury as a result. Emory University School of Medicine professor Dr. Joel Zivot – who was retained by Pike’s legal team as a medical expert – told the BBC that the amount of the lethal drug pentobarbital in her blood likely never reached a level high enough to stop her breathing and heartbeat. “It’s very possible that as a consequence of the delay of the beginning of resuscitation she will have a brain injury,” Zivot explained.

One proposed regulatory change would open up accredited investing to more professional licenses — accountants, financial planners, investment bankers, and research analysts — but also add a new potential way to become an accredited investor: an exam.
